One 16x16 straight conveyor belt tile, authored from the master palette by art/tools/make-factory-parts.mjs. Hand-authored after two paid Retro Diffusion takes came back as a featureless dark rectangle with the run pointing the wrong way. The deciding reason is not quality: a belt tile must repeat along its run with NO SEAM, and a mismatched edge repeats every 16px down a straight line. `tile_x` is a best effort; the modulus in that script is exact, and it asserts left edge equals right edge on every build.

One 16x16 grabber arm, drawn pointing EAST and centred, authored from the master palette by art/tools/make-factory-parts.mjs. Hand-authored after two paid takes returned an inkblot with no claw. One 16x16 tileable diagonal hatch, authored from the master palette by art/tools/make-zone-overlay.mjs and tinted per zone in code. A zone is a plan, not a machine (plan §5), so it reads as an annotation drawn over the world. Hand-authored because it must tile EXACTLY in both axes and must have binary alpha — the cook stage binarises alpha, so a soft wash would come back opaque and bury the field it annotates.

One 7x7 status lamp — a single lit pixel — for the off state (no work cycle at all — the sell bin, a decorative object). Authored from the master palette by art/tools/make-status-lamp.mjs. Seven shapes, one per LampState, because §16 lists colourblind-safe machine status as lamp SHAPE variation rather than colour alone — and the palette makes that urgent rather than optional, since starved amber and blocked red are deliberate neighbours on a warm limited palette and are near-identical under deuteranopia. Still ONE tint per state applied in code (§13), so the batch and the page are unchanged; the shape now carries the state and the colour reinforces it. The generator asserts every pair of shapes differs by at least six of twenty-five pixels, which is the greyscale criterion made mechanical. Core is `paper` so a multiply tint lands on the intended hue; the `ink` halo is what keeps a pale lamp legible on a pale machine. `trim` is false: all seven must sit on the same 7x7 grid or the lamp would jump around the machine as its state changed.

The game's own 6x10 monospaced bitmap font — 104 glyphs on a 32-column grid — authored from the master palette by art/tools/make-ui-font.mjs. §15 puts text-in-sprites on the NEVER list and names a runtime bitmap font as the only sanctioned way to draw text, and says in the same breath not to ask an image model for letterforms. Monospaced on purpose: every site it replaces asked the browser for `ui-monospace`, and a fixed advance means the font publishes NO per-glyph metrics — a cell is index%%32 across and index/32 down, which is the same arithmetic on both sides. Column 5 and row 9 of every cell are an advance gutter so nearest-neighbour sampling at a seam picks up transparency rather than the next letter; the em dash is the one glyph allowed to use all six columns, because that is what an em dash is. Drawn in `paper`, the palette's declared UI-text-on-dark value, and tinted at draw time. `trim` is false — trimming a glyph grid to its overall bounds would slide every cell off the grid, the same reason the crop strips opt out.
